name: Tirzah
title: Daughter of Zelophehad Who Fought for Women's Inheritance Rights
summary: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad from the tribe of Manasseh. She and her sisters brought their case before Moses because their father had died without sons, and they demanded inheritance rights to his land. Their case led to an important law change that granted daughters the right to inherit when there were no sons.

keyEvents.title: Zelophehad's Daughters Present Their Case Before Moses
keyEvents.description: Tirzah and her four sisters stood before Moses, the priest Eleazar, the leaders, and the entire congregation at the entrance to the tent of meeting and demanded their father's inheritance portion, since he had died without sons.

keyEvents.title: The Lord Grants Tirzah and Her Sisters Their Request
keyEvents.description: God told Moses that the daughters of Zelophehad were right and that they should receive their father's inheritance. This became a new law in Israel.

keyEvents.title: A new inheritance law is established for Israel
keyEvents.description: Based on the case of Tirzah and her sisters, the Lord established a general law that inheritance should go to daughters if a man died without sons.

keyEvents.title: The tribal leaders raise questions about inheritance and marriage
keyEvents.description: The leaders of the tribe of Manasseh approached Moses with concern that the inheritance might pass to other tribes if Zelophehad's daughters married outside their tribe.

keyEvents.title: Command to marry within the tribe
keyEvents.description: Moses commanded on the Lord's behalf that Tirzah and her sisters should marry men from their own tribe so that the inheritance would remain in the tribe of Manasseh. They obeyed this and married their cousins.

keyEvents.title: Tirzah and her sisters receive their inheritance in Canaan
keyEvents.description: When the land was distributed under Joshua, Zelophehad's daughters, including Tirzah, came forward and received their inheritance among the tribe of Manasseh, as the Lord had commanded.
